draft.title: Emerging and re-emerging diseases
card: a disease that is new to a human population, or that has spread into a new area. It can come from a new pathogen, or from a known pathogen that has moved to a new host, such as from animals to humans.
a disease that was once under control and has become common again. Measles and tuberculosis are examples.
Air travel, trade, growing cities and closer contact with wild animals help pathogens reach new people. Falling vaccination rates and drug resistance can let old diseases return.

A population with no previous exposure has no immunity to a new pathogen. After Europeans arrived in Australia, diseases such as smallpox, influenza and measles spread among Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples and caused many deaths.
draft.remember: A disease emerges when a population meets it for the first time, and re-emerges when an old one returns.

a.q: Why did diseases brought by Europeans cause so many deaths among Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples?
opts: The population had not been exposed to them before
The pathogens were new types that evolved in Australia
The population had been vaccinated against other diseases
The diseases could not infect any other population
a.why: The pathogens were new to the population, so people had no immunity to them and the diseases spread widely. The pathogens did not evolve in Australia. They were carried here by people arriving from elsewhere.
a.clue: Think about whether people had met these pathogens before.

b.q: Measles was once rare in a region because most children were vaccinated. After vaccination rates fell, cases rose sharply. How is this disease best described?
opts: Re-emerging, because a controlled disease became common again
Emerging, because it is a new pathogen in the region
Emerging, because it passed from animals to humans
Re-emerging, because the pathogen has become a new species
b.why: The disease was already known and under control, then became common again, so it is re-emerging. It is not emerging, because the pathogen was not new to the region and had not moved to a new host.
b.clue: Was the disease new, or had it come back?
